title: Fixing a free variable reduces the free count by one
statement:
Let $\rho$ be a restriction on $n$ variables, let $v$ be a variable that is free under $\rho$, and let $b$ be a Boolean value. Let $\rho'$ be the restriction obtained from $\rho$ by fixing $v$ to the value $b$ and leaving every other variable unchanged. Then the number of free variables of $\rho'$ is one less than the number of free variables of $\rho$; equivalently, if $f(\rho)$ denotes the number of free variables of $\rho$, then
\[
f(\rho') + 1 = f(\rho).
\]
hypotheses_covered: ρ is a restriction on n variables
v is a variable that is free under ρ (ρ(v) unset)
ρ' is ρ updated at v to fix it to b
replaced:
If $\rho\,v = \mathrm{none}$, then updating $\rho$ at $v$ to $\mathrm{some}\,b$
decreases $\mathrm{numFree}$ by exactly one:
$\mathrm{numFree}(\rho[v \mapsto b]) + 1 = \rho.\mathrm{numFree}$.
